chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Zakariyya al-Mu'min, raising it, he said:
Whatever you spend on perfume, it is not extravagance.
ai.seo_question: Is spending money on perfume considered wasteful in Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that expenditure on perfume is not considered *israf* (wastefulness), distinguishing it from frivolous spending by framing it as an act of self-care and social etiquette. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that maintaining a pleasant appearance and scent is a virtuous practice that enhances one's dignity and interaction with others, provided it does not lead to extravagance.

en.hubeali: From him, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Zakariyya Al Momin, raising it,
‘He<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘Whatever you spend regarding the perfume, so it is not an extravagance’.
en.sarwar: 16. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Zakariya al-Mu’min in a marfu‘ manner has said the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Your spending for perfumes is not useless spending. 5 ”
